Bosnia and Herzegovina imposes temporary tariff on imported power transformers

SARAJEVO, June 14 — Bosnia and Herzegovina has imposed a temporary 15% tariff on imported power transformers, government officials said Friday, citing the need to protect domestic producers and stabilize the Electric Utilities industry. The measure, which took effect Monday, is expected to last for at least six months while authorities assess its impact.

The tariff affects all transformer imports, including those used for grid upgrades and new renewable energy projects. The Ministry of Foreign Trade said in a statement the decision was made after a surge in cheaper transformer imports over the past year, which “threatened the viability of local manufacturing and jeopardized ongoing infrastructure investments.”

Industry representatives welcomed the move. “This measure will give local manufacturers time to adjust and ensure that vital upgrades to the national grid are not derailed by unfair competition,” said Adnan Koric, spokesperson for the Bosnia and Herzegovina Electric Utilities Association.

However, utility operators warned the tariff could delay some ongoing projects. “We are concerned about increased costs and possible bottlenecks in transformer supply, especially for planned substation expansions,” said Edina Smajlovic, head of operations at Energoline Holdings. “We are monitoring the situation closely.”

Analysts noted that transformer prices have risen by up to 12% since the tariff was introduced, with some utilities reportedly seeking to renegotiate contracts. The Ministry has pledged to review the policy in September, but for now, the Electric Utilities industry is adjusting to the new trade environment as the measure remains in force.
